correctness.rationale: Every group term in pure parameter-free group language is an integer linear combination. A tuple type is exactly the kernel of R^k->C_(p²)⊕C_p, R=Z/p². The possible quotients are 1,C_p,C_(p²),C_p²,A_p; epimorphisms divided by subgroup automorphisms give kernel counts 1,u_k,p^(k-1)u_k,v_k,w_k. The embedded quotient may split into 1,2,1,p+1,1 global automorphism orbits due to characteristic pA_p⊂A_p[p], giving O=T+u+pv. Unary pA_p distinguishes automorphism invariant versus quantifier-free; all abelian groups order<8 are cyclic or C2². Independently constructed full linear-equation truth vectors and all global automorphism orbits for 1340 tuples at (2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,1),(3,2); reproduced (T,O)=(3,4),(14,19),(85,106),(3,4),(22,29). Finite checks support, but do not replace, all-p/all-k counting proof.

originality.rationale: Existing quantifier-free definability theorems give semantic preservation algorithms, and existing finite-abelian-p-group automorphism descriptions give matrix groups. The assessed combination produces explicit all-prime/all-arity counts of kernels vs global embedding orbits and the least unary obstruction. The routine Nakayama and Gaussian coefficients are credited as tools, not standalone novelty.

value.rationale: Quantifier-free versus automorphism-invariant relations is a substantive finite-model-theoretic distinction. The mixed-exponent rank-two p-group is the first natural abelian obstruction, and explicit all-k orbit spectra and exact size-eight unary threshold quantify that gap, useful for definability tests and algebraic orbit enumeration.

limitations: Pure group language with parameters forbidden, no quantifiers; not a statement about all finite abelian groups or higher-order model theory.
